message.content: ATP synthase (also called F₁F₀‑ATPase) is the enzyme that produces the bulk of cellular ATP in mitochondria. It uses the proton gradient generated by the electron transport chain to drive the phosphorylation of ADP to ATP. The enzyme is embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane; the F₀ portion forms a proton channel that allows protons to flow back into the matrix, and the F₁ portion contains the catalytic sites where ADP + Pi are converted to ATP. In short, ATP synthase couples the energy stored in the proton motive force to the synthesis of ATP, making it the key enzyme of oxidative phosphorylation.
